assumptions: Ramu canonical history FY22-FY26 (revenue 330/365/405/450/500, PAT 30/34/39/44/50, EPS 3.00-5.00, 10 cr shares)
Lab A jumpy what-if: revenue 330,440,330,400,500 (one-off, revenue only)
Lab B: constant growth rate from ₹500 cr FY26 revenue; simple line adds same rupees each year
Lab C: one-off paths from 500: steady 550/605; 375/500; 375/450; 250/500
Lab D: profit 50, 10 cr shares, issue price ₹100 (canonical), profit growth is the reader's assumption and ignores returns on new money
Defaults canonical: A FY22→FY26 revenue; B 11%/7y; C bad year+rebound; D +15% (FY27E PAT 57.5) and 0 new shares. Lab D default has no gap by design (canonical); presets show it
lab.independent_calculation_method: labtest.py (scratchpad): Python oracle computing CAGR, averages, compounding, doubling, base-effect and EPS from first principles, compared with window.cagrResults/labResults/baseResults/dilResults in Chromium via Playwright
lab.tolerance: 1e-9 absolute for growth rates; 1e-6 relative for compounded rupee values
invariants: average of yearly rates >= CAGR (360-case run includes gap>=0 for every start/end/metric)
EPS growth = profit growth when no new shares
lab.axis_and_clipping: Lab B y-axis rescales to max(final, simple, 1000) with the top value printed; x ticks 0, n/2, n. Lab D axis +-m with m>=20. No clipping.
lab.deviation: Lab A: with Ramu's steady actuals the gap between average and CAGR is ~0.00 points; the jumpy what-if and lab C show the gap. Plan states 4-year revenue CAGR 11.0%; exact 10.9466%, shown as 10.95%.
